report:
PASS for the explicitly scoped sufficient-condition alternative: scalar Hopf targets H_n, n≥3, with ambient data pulled back from projective space as stated. This does not resolve unrestricted P18. The supplied candidate=false and the statements leaving unrestricted P18 open are compatible with success under the alternative completion criterion. Prior verdicts, reading flags, hashes and source-application judgments were not used as mathematical premises.

A. The higher-dimensional BMP argument is valid. Direct differentiation gives n−2 angular entries (μ+V_x)/μ and the stated radial/fiber block. The radial contribution of V_x vanishes because the radial Hessian of x=log|ξ|² vanishes; this accounts for the apparent cancellation in the form expansion. With A=μ+V_x and Δ=(μ+V_xx)(1+V_wbarw)−|μ+V_xbarw|², the actual angularly integrated density is J_n=2n(n−1)A^(n−2)Δ. Consequently J_n=[n(n−1)/6]A^(n−3)J_3. The normalized radial Fubini–Study density and fiber integral two give the stated constants, including background mass 2n when a=b=1.

The required family, unchanged heat scale, strict positivity, endpoint extensions and slope estimates are present in [Xia–Zhang](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.21053v1). Dividing the source forms and operator by 2π leaves the scalar potentials unchanged. On x<0, exact fiber integration gives 12(μ+g′)[g″+μ(1−μ)]. Its integral is bounded by 3/2+24m, since 0<μ+g′≤μ and ∫|g″|≤2m. Thus divergence occurs on x≥0, where A≥1/4 for small η. The density comparison proves divergence in every n≥3. The cold proof’s alternative localization to x≥−2 also works: the negative tail has fixed integrated mass, while A has a uniform positive lower bound on the remaining region. Both arguments give genuinely smooth, strictly admissible global potentials. Scaling against h≥c(α+β) proves BMP failure for every Hermitian h. Neither argument establishes positive lower mass.

B. Both extraction proofs are valid independently. In the author’s proof, the auxiliary spaces can be taken as reduced main components of proper fiber products. They are compact analytic spaces and preserve the existing smooth neighborhood of generic D. Proper mapping makes each divisor image analytic. Blowing up its reduced ideal is smooth over the smooth part of the center. A minimum-order generator pulls back as z_1^m times a unit, so the indicated quotients give a holomorphic generic lift. Resolving the target preserves that lift because [Włodarczyk’s resolution](https://gokovagt.org/proceedings/2008/ggt08-wlodarczyk.pdf) is an isomorphism over the entire smooth locus. The exact Jacobian identity gives J_new=J_old−(c−1)m≥0. Every codimension-at-least-two step therefore decreases a finite nonnegative integer. Termination yields a divisor image; an originally proper image cannot become horizontal.

The cold proof instead prepares a smooth compact target center and principalizes the pulled center ideals on the source. The [Bierstone–Milman compact analytic results](https://www.mahalex.net/teaching/seminars/gabber/Bierstone-Milman%20Canonical%20desingularization%20in%20characteristic%20zero.pdf) supply finite operations. Preparation is unchanged over the original smooth center. Near generic D the pulled ideal is already a power of its equation times a unit; a smooth blowup center containing generic D can only be that divisor, whose blowup is an isomorphism. Hence source principalization preserves the generic neighborhood. The same Jacobian decrease proves termination. This validates that proof without substituting the author’s target-resolution method.

At the terminal divisor, tangential dominance gives the normal form (z_1,…,z_d,z′)↦(z_1^e,z_2,…,z_d). Generic factorization of ideal generators proves the order identity with one fixed e for every test ideal. Divisorial subtraction is interpreted through currents and genuine residual representatives, rather than pointwise subtraction of two infinite values. At very general F the residual has zero point Lelong number. Skoda and Hölder with |y_1|^(2/e−2) prove integrability of every finite exponential weight after ramification. A positive residual divisor coefficient would contradict that integrability. This covers R|_F≡−∞. The cold proof’s ball-image growth estimate also proves zero residual coefficient. Horizontal divisors are handled by generic submersion coordinates. Both identities therefore hold with the required quantifiers.

C. The submersion multiplier-ideal proof works for every real t>0. Fubini proves the extended-base inclusion; fiber Taylor estimates put each coefficient of an integrable germ in the base ideal. Taylor truncations and Krull intersection give membership in the actual convergent local ideal. Taking the quotient defining Y yields a_t=q* b_t, rather than replacing the image ideal by a multiplier ideal of a naive restriction. Product coordinates also give ν(p*U,Y)=ν(U,B)=0.

D. The closed-base argument establishes the positive-mass antecedent before using divisorial convergence. For a sufficiently large a, the common normalized competitor z is aκ/2-psh and lies below w. Expanding its aκ product supplies the smooth term (a/2)^d; closed mass monotonicity transfers the lower bound to w. Bounded truncations and Stokes give the upper bound a^d. The decreasing potentials w_j are ordinary models and retain the analytic ideal coefficients. The positive-mass conclusion of [Darvas–Xia, Proposition 2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.08259v2) consequently gives ν(w,F)=lim_j 2^(−j)ord_F(b_(2^j))=τ_B(F) for every divisor over B. Its definition includes arbitrary proper smooth bimeromorphic models. No BMP theorem is applied on the Hopf target.

The cold base proof also checks: analytic comparison follows by resolving the global coherent ideal and bounding the residual after divisorial subtraction. The envelopes form a decreasing, nontrivial sequence of models. Their analytic masses are at least (a−K)^d. The model mass-convergence theorem first gives positive limit mass and then gives divisorial convergence. Thus neither proof replaces the necessary model theorem by ordinary L¹ semicontinuity.

For each target modification and each prime D, extraction supplies the same multiplicity in the ideal and Lelong formulas. Hence the single potential q*w realizes every target coefficient simultaneously. Elliptic invariance concerns the entire competitor family. The envelope descends through local sections, and basic Ω_(a,b)-positivity is equivalent to aκ-positivity. Every base modification lifts to a smooth compact fiber product; the prime over F is irreducible and has multiplicity one. These detect every base constraint and prove the full envelope identity. The cold fiber-maximum proof also checks every competitor: finite maxima retain the constraints, and a common genuine lower bound permits passage to the canonical limit on each modification. Enlarging Ω gives exactness by the stated sandwich.

E. The mass formula uses actual bounded products. At truncation level, horizontal degree d and β²=0 give (Ω_(a,b)+dd^c q*v_j)^n=nb β∧q*(aκ+dd^c v_j)^d. Restricting to {v>−j} and taking the non-pluripolar limit gives mass 2nb times the base mass, with the claimed positive finite bounds. This uses only the bounded construction in [BGL §2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.01090); its BMP-dependent unbounded construction is unnecessary here.

The compatible type is an ideal type. The cold n1 proof of the divisorial ideal criterion is valid: Bergman ideal slopes recover divisorial Lelong numbers; global principalization gives analytic comparison; strong openness and the weighted approximation inclusions yield ideal inclusion at every real weight. Thus equal profiles identify all-real-weight ideals. This independently validates the author’s closed-base application, followed by the actual submersion ideal identity. Addition concerns ideal classes in backgrounds admitting the sums, rather than equality of normalized sum envelopes. Positive scaling also follows directly from the competitor bijection. Fixedness is among the task-granted background conclusions and is additionally consistent with maximality of the full profile envelope.

Full ordinary obstacle envelopes commute with basic pullback: the fiber action preserves each finite obstacle and its comparison constant, and ordinary order descends by surjectivity, including canonical pole values. The dyadic pulled models therefore decrease to the full trace. On every modification they have the genuine limiting pullback as an integrable lower bound, giving L¹ convergence. Extraction with fixed F and e gives convergence of every modified divisorial coefficient. These conclusions establish neither ordinary-type independence across backgrounds nor extremal singularity-volume convergence.

F. In d ambient normal variables, a germ of least degree k is integrable precisely when k>t−d. This gives max(floor(t−d+1),0), including the logarithmically divergent boundary weights. Taking the actual image on B gives m_P to that power, and division by t gives ord_D(q*m_P) on every model. The displayed genuine logarithmic potential realizes all these orders. On the point blowup its residual smooth form has class aH−F. Since H^d=1, mixed H/F intersections vanish and F^d=(−1)^(d−1), its actual non-pluripolar mass is a^d−1. Fiber integration gives 2nb(a^d−1). Equality with the normalized trace envelope is not implied.

The geometry also checks directly: H_n≅S^(2n−1)×S¹, β has fiber integral two, Ω_(a,b) is Hermitian and dΩ_(a,b)=−b dr∧α. Non-Kählerness follows either from b₁=1 or from H²=0 and Stokes. The projective base dimension is at least two, and arbitrary nonanalytic ambient data, including infinite naive restrictions, are allowed. This exceeds the supplied curve-base and analytic-product examples. The known envelope, fixedness, intrinsic calculus and closed-target conclusions should be credited as background; literature priority is not established.

Harmless wording correction: the historical private note’s heading saying every diagonal Hopf manifold should say every scalar Hopf H_n. The operative theorem uses equal scalar multipliers throughout. The July18-to-October4 bibliography edit is mathematically neutral. I could not retrieve the final SGPT PDF here, so I do not certify that edition’s date, numbering or bytes. The indispensable mathematical statements were checked in the accessible primary papers cited above and below; the supplied assertion of earlier retrieval was not used as evidence. No substantial mathematical repair is required.
